review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner (self-review, not independent approval)
review.decision: Keep a bounded recent Codex parse snapshot instead of discarding a large session cache entirely
review.notes: Read-only current-session measurements found300 turns/~25.8MB serialized, cold Load1.77s and a repeat1.16s; source retains up to800 turns then drops a cache entry above32MiB. New code must bound retention while streaming and across append resumes, keep full individual turn content and original ordinals/record IDs, expose omitted prefix via existing count/cursor contracts, and keep source history recoverable. No real-session mutation, transcript copy, cache-limit increase or production deployment. Existing cache/history tests stay unchanged. Current-session timing is not a synthetic benchmark or device/UI acceptance; the first /usr/bin/time wrapper returned1 only because sandbox denied sysctl after the probe finished, and a direct rerun exited0; preserve both records. Refined before production implementation: raw requests for300 turns must still return all available requested turns; only the stored cache may keep a bounded whole-turn tail. A later request for20 may hit that tail, but a request beyond cached coverage must reparse rather than silently return fewer turns. App recent-window endpoint must opt in separately. The first fixture accidentally expected trailing whitespace removed by existing transcript normalization; preserve that fixture failure and correct the synthetic string, not production normalization.

cases.description: Large Codex history keeps a bounded reusable recent cache and lossless source history access
cases.setup: Isolated Codex rollout with enough complete public turns to exceed the existing32MiB retention budget, a fresh Loader and exact source-based history cursor; no real HOME/session data
cases.action: Read a large300-turn request and retain its bounded cached tail; repeat with20 newest turns, then request300 again, append a complete turn and read20, and page into the omitted prefix using source history
cases.expected: The full300-turn request returns every available requested complete turn unchanged, while a cache entry remains within32MiB by retaining only whole recent turns. An unchanged20-turn read reuses that entry rather than rescanning; a later300-turn request beyond its coverage returns full requested history by parsing again, never falsely claims a complete cache hit. Latest content, original ordinals and record IDs remain exact. Append resumes safely when coverage suffices and preserves prior returned snapshots; older source turns remain readable by valid cursor and reads never modify source bytes. A single individually oversized turn stays complete even if uncached. Old behavior must fail the large-entry-retained assertion, not normalization/setup/timeout. No global history truncation or cache budget increase.
